## Summary (human-written)
<!-- Write this yourself, not with an AI tool. 2-5 sentences: the problem, why
     this approach, and what you checked yourself. -->


Part **12/n** of the Kimi K3 / Dist-MoE training stack. Stacked on
[#5684](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5684); next:
[#5686](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5686).

## Why

Shared experts do not depend on routed-expert dispatch/computation. Serial
execution cannot overlap them; an unordered side stream can read unfinished
inputs/outputs or recycled storage. This opt-in records input readiness before
routed launches and explicitly joins shared completion before output addition,
without changing model or autograd construction order.

**Example.**

```python
from dataclasses import replace

# CUDA, TP=1, with shared experts; serial remains the default.
moe_config = replace(moe_config, overlap_shared_experts=True)
```

```text
caller: input-ready -> router / routed experts -> wait shared -> add
             |                                      ^
shared:      +-------> shared experts ---------------+
```

## What changed

- Ordinary MoE and Kimi's latent MoE use the same event/stream boundary.
- Protect input/output allocator lifetimes across streams, avoiding allocator
  operations on recompute placeholders.
- Retain serial defaults; reject missing shared experts, CPU inputs, and TP>1.
- Supply an opt-in recipe override and documentation next to the MoE code.

## Alternatives considered

- Launching on an unordered stream risks data races and use-after-recycle.
- Waiting for routed completion before starting shared work removes overlap.
- Reordering Python branches changes autograd construction unnecessarily.
- Unconditional overlap adds activation memory without proving a speedup.

## User-facing changes

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Shared experts execute serially after routed experts. | The opt-in forks after input readiness and joins before addition. |
| No shared-stream policy exists. | Serial remains default; unsupported opt-in modes raise. |

## Numerics and testing

Fresh retained-parent checks: **153 CPU tests plus 14 subtests** and **six
GPU-0-only tests** pass.

| Native GPU check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Ordinary/latent MoE, with and without FullAC, twelve eager updates | Exact outputs, losses, norms, input gradients, all parameter gradients/updates versus serial. |
| Latent MoE, with and without FullAC, five changing-input graph updates | Exact output, loss, gradients, and updates versus serial. |

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' python -m pytest -q -o addopts= --tb=short \
  tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/common/test_moe.py \
  tests/unit_tests/cpu/recipes/test_shared_expert_overlap.py \
  tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/common/test_dist_moe.py \
  tests/unit_tests/cpu/test_trainer.py

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8 \
python -m pytest -q -o addopts= --tb=short \
  tests/unit_tests/gpu/models/common/test_shared_expert_overlap.py
```

All non-type hooks pass. Deterministic execution is strict; assertions,
tolerances, and the nonfatal PyTorch AccumulateGrad stream warning were not
weakened or suppressed. Historical distributed EP/FSDP checks are not fresh
results from this one-GPU review.

## Landing gates

This is an independent candidate alongside the still-open
[#5554](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5554). Maintainers should
choose one implementation; duplicate overlap implementations should not land.
The two full-scale recipe ports do not enable this optional policy, so their
historical throughput is not evidence of an overlap gain.

Fresh distributed FSDP/EP overlap and full-scale throughput remain unverified.
Whole-model compilation and GraphTrainer parallel-branch lowering are outside
this policy. Final-tip type checking and maintainer review/CI are still needed.

<details>
<summary>Draft stack — review and land in this order</summary>

1/n (#5674) is merged. 2/n (#5675) was closed because the validated recipes do not use its prefetch-disable policy; it is no longer in the stack.

| Position | Draft PR |
| --- | --- |
| 3/n | [#5676 — [fsdp] 3/n Support layer-scoped CPU offload](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5676) |
| 4/n | [#5677 — [optim] 4/n Bound optimizer memory ownership and allocation lifetimes](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5677) |
| 5/n | [#5678 — [dist_muon] 5/n Support CP and TP storage-to-compute layouts](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5678) |
| 6/n | [#5679 — [profiler] 6/n Preserve active failures during shutdown](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5679) |
| 7/n | [#5680 — [attention] 7/n Keep linear-attention graph metadata replayable](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5680) |
| 8/n | [#5681 — [cp] 8/n Apply the Ulysses NCCL safeguard to compact and linear attention](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5681) |
| 9/n | [#5682 — [compile] 9/n Compile MLA assembly and router postprocessing](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5682) |
| 10/n | [#5683 — [pp] 10/n Add once-only startup cache release](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5683) |
| 11/n | [#5684 — [dist_moe] 11/n Enable Kimi K3 SiTU-GLU training and pipeline lifecycle](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5684) |
| 12/n | [#5685 — [moe] 12/n Add opt-in shared-expert CUDA stream overlap](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5685) |
| 13/n | [#5686 — [ac] 13/n Add block-scoped activation retention](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5686) |
| 14/n | Full-scale 256-GB300 and 512-GB200 MXFP8 recipes; separate draft PR being prepared |

</details>

+# Copyright (c) Meta Platforms, Inc. and affiliates.

+# LICENSE file in the root directory of this source tree.
+
+"""The shared-expert override preserves ordinary and latent model ownership."""
+
+from dataclasses import replace
+
+import pytest
+
+from torchtitan.models.common.moe import MoE
+from torchtitan.models.kimi_k3.moe import KimiLatentMoE
+from torchtitan_recipes.overrides.shared_expert_overlap import shared_expert_overlap
+from torchtitan_recipes.tests.models.deepseek_v3 import deepseek_v3_debugmodel
+from torchtitan_recipes.tests.models.kimi_k3 import kimi_k3_debugmodel
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("latent", [False, True])
+def test_shared_overlap_override_preserves_layout(latent: bool) -> None:
+    """The opt-in keeps router/expert configs shared, including Kimi's latent path."""
+    model = (kimi_k3_debugmodel() if latent else deepseek_v3_debugmodel()).model
+    config = next(
+        moe
+        for _, moe, _, _ in model.traverse(MoE.Config)
+        if isinstance(moe, KimiLatentMoE.Config) == latent
+        and moe.shared_experts is not None
+    )
+    actual = shared_expert_overlap(config)
+    assert type(actual) is type(config)
+    assert actual.overlap_shared_experts
+    assert not config.overlap_shared_experts
+    assert actual.routed_experts is config.routed_experts
+    assert actual.shared_experts is config.shared_experts
+    assert actual.router is config.router
+    unshared = replace(config, shared_experts=None)
+    assert shared_expert_overlap(unshared) is unshared

+# Copyright (c) Meta Platforms, Inc. and affiliates.
+# All rights reserved.
+#
+# This source code is licensed under the BSD-style license found in the
+# LICENSE file in the root directory of this source tree.
+
+"""Exact numerical checks for shared-expert CUDA stream scheduling."""
+
+from copy import deepcopy
+from dataclasses import replace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from torchtitan.distributed.activation_remat import FullActivationRematConfig
+from torchtitan.models.base.module import Module, ModuleDict
+from torchtitan.models.common.activation import Sigmoid, SiTUGLU
+from torchtitan.models.common.feed_forward import DenseFeedForward
+from torchtitan.models.common.linear import GroupedLinear, Linear
+from torchtitan.models.common.linear.hi_mid_lo_linear import HiMidLoLinear
+from torchtitan.models.common.moe import MoE, RoutedExperts, TokenChoiceTopKRouter
+from torchtitan.models.common.moe.token_dispatcher import LocalTokenDispatcher
+from torchtitan.models.common.nn_modules import RMSNorm
+from torchtitan.models.kimi_k3.moe import KimiLatentMoE
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def deterministic_numerics():
+    """Use strict deterministic execution for eager and graph comparisons."""
+    torch.manual_seed(42)
+    previous = torch.are_deterministic_algorithms_enabled()
+    torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(previous)
+
+
+def _moe_config(*, latent: bool) -> MoE.Config:
+    """Build shared and learned-router branches with a reduced SiTU-GLU FFN."""
+    dim, expert_dim, hidden_dim, num_experts = 128, 64 if latent else 128, 128, 4
+    values = dict(
+        num_experts=num_experts,
+        load_balance_coeff=None,
+        router=TokenChoiceTopKRouter.Config(
+            num_experts=num_experts,
+            gate=HiMidLoLinear.Config(in_features=dim, out_features=num_experts),
+            score_func=Sigmoid.Config(),
+            top_k=2,
+            route_norm=True,
+        ),
+        routed_experts=RoutedExperts.Config(
+            w13=GroupedLinear.Config(
+                group_size=num_experts,
+                in_features=expert_dim,
+                out_features=hidden_dim,
+                num_linears=2,
+            ),
+            w2=GroupedLinear.Config(
+                group_size=num_experts,
+                in_features=hidden_dim,
+                out_features=expert_dim,
+            ),
+            token_dispatcher=LocalTokenDispatcher.Config(
+                num_experts=num_experts, top_k=2
+            ),
+            activation_fn=SiTUGLU.Config(beta=4.0, linear_beta=25.0),
+        ),
+        shared_experts=DenseFeedForward.Config(
+            w13=Linear.Config(in_features=dim, out_features=hidden_dim, num_linears=2),
+            w2=Linear.Config(in_features=hidden_dim, out_features=dim),
+            activation_fn=SiTUGLU.Config(beta=4.0, linear_beta=25.0),
+        ),
+    )
+    if latent:
+        return KimiLatentMoE.Config(
+            **values,
+            routed_down=Linear.Config(in_features=dim, out_features=expert_dim),
+            routed_norm=RMSNorm.Config(normalized_shape=expert_dim),
+            routed_up=Linear.Config(in_features=expert_dim, out_features=dim),
+        )
+    return MoE.Config(**values)
+
+
+class _Block(Module):
+    def __init__(self, config: MoE.Config):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.moe = config.build()
+
+    def forward(self, x_TD: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return self.moe(x_TD)
+
+
+class _Model(Module):
+    def __init__(self, config: MoE.Config):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.layers = ModuleDict({"0": _Block(config)})
+
+    def forward(self, x_TD: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return self.layers["0"](x_TD)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="requires CUDA")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("latent", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("checkpoint", [False, True])
+def test_shared_overlap_preserves_exact_training(
+    latent: bool, checkpoint: bool
+) -> None:
+    """Twelve deterministic updates preserve exact outputs, norms and gradients."""
+    torch.manual_seed(42)
+    previous_deterministic = torch.are_deterministic_algorithms_enabled()
+    torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)
+    try:
+        config = _moe_config(latent=latent)
+        serial = _Model(config).cuda().bfloat16()
+        overlapped = (
+            _Model(replace(config, overlap_shared_experts=True)).cuda().bfloat16()
+        )
+        # GroupedLinear and RMSNorm parameters are initialized via init_states.
+        with torch.no_grad():
+            for parameter in serial.parameters():
+                parameter.uniform_(-0.05, 0.05)
+        overlapped.load_state_dict(deepcopy(serial.state_dict()))
+        if checkpoint:
+            FullActivationRematConfig().apply(serial)
+            FullActivationRematConfig().apply(overlapped)
+        streams = {}
+
+        def shared_forward(module, args):
+            streams["shared"] = torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream
+
+        def routed_forward(module, args):
+            streams["routed"] = torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream
+
+        handles = [
+            overlapped.layers["0"].moe.shared_experts.register_forward_pre_hook(
+                shared_forward
+            ),
+            overlapped.layers["0"].moe.routed_experts.register_forward_pre_hook(
+                routed_forward
+            ),
+        ]
+        for _ in range(12):
+            input_TD = torch.randn(32, 128, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+            results = []
+            for model in (serial, overlapped):
+                model.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
+                x_TD = input_TD.detach().clone().requires_grad_(True)
+                output_TD = model(x_TD)
+                loss = output_TD.float().square().mean()
+                loss.backward()
+                norm = torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0)
+                results.append((output_TD.detach(), loss.detach(), norm, x_TD.grad))
+                del output_TD, loss
+            torch.cuda.synchronize()
+            assert streams["shared"] != streams["routed"]
+            assert streams["routed"] == torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream
+            for actual, expected in zip(results[1], results[0], strict=True):
+                torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+            for actual, expected in zip(
+                overlapped.parameters(), serial.parameters(), strict=True
+            ):
+                assert actual.grad is not None and expected.grad is not None
+                torch.testing.assert_close(actual.grad, expected.grad, rtol=0, atol=0)
+                with torch.no_grad():
+                    actual.add_(actual.grad, alpha=-0.01)
+                    expected.add_(expected.grad, alpha=-0.01)
+        for handle in handles:
+            handle.remove()
+    finally:
+        torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(previous_deterministic)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="requires CUDA")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("checkpoint", [False, True])
+def test_shared_overlap_cuda_graph_replay(checkpoint: bool) -> None:
+    """Five changing-input updates match serial outputs and every gradient."""
+    torch.manual_seed(42)
+    model = _Model(replace(_moe_config(latent=True), overlap_shared_experts=True))
+    model = model.cuda().bfloat16()
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        for parameter in model.parameters():
+            parameter.uniform_(-0.05, 0.05)
+    if checkpoint:
+        FullActivationRematConfig().apply(model)
+    serial = _Model(_moe_config(latent=True)).cuda().bfloat16()
+    serial.load_state_dict(deepcopy(model.state_dict()))
+    if checkpoint:
+        FullActivationRematConfig().apply(serial)
+    x_TD = torch.randn(32, 128, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, requires_grad=True)
+    parameters = tuple(model.parameters())
+
+    def forward_backward():
+        output_TD = model(x_TD)
+        loss = output_TD.float().square().mean()
+        gradients = torch.autograd.grad(loss, (x_TD, *parameters))
+        return output_TD, loss, *gradients
+
+    warmup = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    warmup.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+    with torch.cuda.stream(warmup):
+        for _ in range(3):
+            forward_backward()
+    torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(warmup)
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        actual = forward_backward()
+    for _ in range(5):
+        with torch.no_grad():
+            x_TD.copy_(torch.randn_like(x_TD))
+        graph.replay()
+        reference_TD = x_TD.detach().clone().requires_grad_(True)
+        expected_output = serial(reference_TD)
+        expected_loss = expected_output.float().square().mean()
+        expected_gradients = torch.autograd.grad(
+            expected_loss, (reference_TD, *serial.parameters())
+        )
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        for candidate, expected in zip(
+            actual, (expected_output, expected_loss, *expected_gradients), strict=True
+        ):
+            torch.testing.assert_close(candidate, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        with torch.no_grad():

+# Shared-expert stream overlap
+
+`MoE.Config.overlap_shared_experts=True` runs shared experts on a CUDA side
+stream. The default is serial execution. The opt-in requires shared experts,
+CUDA inputs and TP=1; unsupported configurations raise. Ordinary MoE and Kimi's
+latent MoE use the same stream boundary.
+
+```python
+from dataclasses import replace
+
+moe_config = replace(moe_config, overlap_shared_experts=True)
+```
+
+The host still constructs router, routed experts, shared experts and output
+addition in their original order. An input-readiness event recorded before
+routed work lets the shared stream start without waiting for routed completion:
+
+```text
+caller stream:  input-ready -> router / routed experts -> wait shared -> add
+                    |                                      ^
+shared stream:      +-------> shared experts ---------------+
+```
+
+This does not guarantee simultaneous execution or an end-to-end speedup.
+Host launch timing and available GPU resources determine actual overlap;
+measure it rather than treating a configured stream as performance evidence.
+
+The enclosing FSDP boundary establishes parameter readiness before the input
+event. Explicit event/stream waits establish shared input readiness and output
+completion. `record_stream` protects allocator lifetime for inputs and outputs,
+including no-grad forwards. Recompute placeholders must not receive allocator
+operations; during checkpoint replay the explicit join and checkpoint lifetime
+keep recomputed tensors live. Autograd executes a branch's backward on its
+forward stream.
+
+Warm up on the final CUDA device before capture to create the module's stream.
+Capture retains the fork/join dependencies; replay does not reconstruct them
+from Python. The policy does not alter routing, activation arithmetic, parameter
+layout or the expert backend's activation-slot contract. It may increase peak
+activation memory because the two branches can be live simultaneously.
+
+The recipe override `torchtitan_recipes.overrides.shared_expert_overlap` enables
+the policy on supported MoE configs and leaves no-shared-expert configs unchanged.
+Whole-model compilation and GraphTrainer parallel-branch lowering are not
+provided by this policy.

+
+"""Opt-in CUDA stream overlap for MoE shared experts."""
+
+from dataclasses import replace
+
+from torchtitan.config import override
+from torchtitan.models.common.moe import MoE
+
+
+@override(target=MoE.Config)
+def shared_expert_overlap(config: MoE.Config) -> MoE.Config:
+    """Enable shared/routed overlap without changing parameter ownership."""
+    if config.shared_experts is None:
+        return config
+    return replace(config, overlap_shared_experts=True)
